recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not revert _profile to uri for FHIR-24918, because doing so would conflict with the later final FHIR-30514 decision and with current versioned canonical search guidance. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for the seed.
issue_request: FHIR-24918 was Published/Persuasive for R5. It reported that _profile appeared as reference in resource.html and generated search-parameter artifacts, while the Common Parameters summary table showed uri and the primitive type cross-map did not map canonical to reference or uri. The resolution requested _profile be shown as uri in resource.html and resource representations, and canonical be shown as mappable to uri.
initial_application: Commit 7c0e9a614fb69e905643cedd0692b2e1f82d149a initially applied GF#24918/GF#24919 by changing the historical Resource spreadsheet _profile row from reference to uri and adding a history entry. That shows the original resolution was applied before later search semantics were revisited.
additional_context: Later Published/Persuasive FHIR-30514 required _profile to be marked reference everywhere because reference and uri differ for versioned canonical values. Commits a1cf2cf018130744adb32d8d92f03de8e16f1a93 and 6d75b061edb768cac1c186923ab8cd4510c2f42f applied that later decision to the Search page and active Resource-_profile SearchParameter source. FHIR-33203 was retracted after confirming PR #1377 applied the _profile part, and FHIR-52936 later clarified that canonical can be used with both uri and reference search types while reference is generally preferred for versioned canonical values.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current source/resource/bundle-Resource-search-params.xml defines Resource-_profile as type reference, and source/search.html says _profile is a reference type parameter and lists it as reference in the common-parameters table. The current search-type mapping and uri prose include canonical under uri as well as reference, so the remaining canonical mapping concern is not a current defect.
